body:
## Problem Statement

The ITDD control plane has proven several bounded components, but it is not yet a complete usable system. A disrupted execution can fail closed while leaving the human without a supported way to abandon the failed run, preserve its forensic record, reconstruct durable project authority, invalidate stale execution authority, and begin a clean execution. Maintenance and human-only break-glass are also specified but unimplemented or unproven. The executable project-local skill workflow lacks complete runtime registration and controller-owned acceptance evidence.

## Solution

Complete the existing control plane in place. Add explicit, human-authorized lifecycle operations for interruption, failure, abandonment, recovery, restart, maintenance, and break-glass. Preserve immutable intent and append-only history, archive every superseded attempt, revoke stale capabilities, dispose of only disposable worker material, reconstruct derived state from verified project-local durable records, and create fresh execution identities. Keep project-aware controller sessions separate from bounded isolated BUILD, TEST, and VERIFY workers. Complete and prove the project-local workflow and demonstrate the finished system from a clean environment.

## User Stories

1. As a human operator, I want a disrupted worker recorded as `INTERRUPTED`, so that worker death never becomes an implicit success.
2. As a human operator, I want failed executions recorded as `FAILED`, so that failures remain distinguishable from interruption and abandonment.
3. As a human operator, I want to explicitly abandon a broken execution, so that I can move forward without pretending it succeeded.
4. As a human operator, I want abandonment to preserve intent, events, evidence, telemetry, outputs, identities, and Git history, so that the failure remains reconstructable.
5. As a human operator, I want stale capabilities and execution authority invalidated during recovery, so that an old worker cannot resume or mutate the new run.
6. As a human operator, I want recovery to remove or quarantine only disposable worker workspaces and derived projections, so that durable authority is not destroyed.
7. As a human operator, I want recovery to reconstruct state from project-local durable authority, so that a fresh process does not depend on conversation history.
8. As a human operator, I want recovery to create new execution identities, so that old evidence and authority cannot be reused.
9. As a human operator, I want recovery to be idempotent and interruption-safe, so that retrying recovery does not duplicate or erase history.
10. As a human operator, I want recovery to require no manual `.idd/` deletion, so that the controller owns its lifecycle.
11. As a human operator, I want recovery to finish at a reconstructed `READY` state, so that starting BUILD remains an explicit action.
12. As a human operator, I want to start BUILD only after explicit confirmation, so that recovery cannot accidentally launch work.
13. As a human operator, I want immutable intent and historical graph versions preserved, so that execution recovery cannot rewrite authority.
14. As a human operator, I want maintenance mode to freeze normal execution, so that controller repair cannot race ordinary work.
15. As a human operator, I want maintenance to preserve the known-good controller and state snapshot, so that repair remains reversible.
16. As a human operator, I want maintenance repair to run in a dedicated environment with regression and recovery proof, so that repaired control code is independently checked.
17. As a human operator, I want human-only break-glass available when normal maintenance cannot operate, so that a defective controller cannot permanently deadlock the project.
18. As a human operator, I want break-glass to record controller SHA, nonce, reason, snapshot, and activation approval, so that emergency authority is auditable.
19. As a human operator, I want old approvals and capabilities invalidated after maintenance or break-glass, so that authority cannot cross controller versions.
20. As a human operator, I want BUILD, TEST, and VERIFY workers to remain fresh, isolated, and least-authority, so that recovery does not weaken execution security.
21. As a controller, I want worker lifecycle outcomes and evidence bound to execution identities, so that stale or false results cannot advance state.
22. As a project maintainer, I want the project-local skill files registered and executable through the intended workflow, so that documented skills are real system behavior.
23. As an implementer, I want `/wayfinder`, `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets`, `/implement`, `/tdd`, and `/code-review` to have controller-compatible boundaries, so that implementation follows the approved lifecycle.
24. As an independent verifier, I want standards and specification review provenance kept separate, so that implementation cannot self-certify.
25. As an independent verifier, I want clean-environment lifecycle tests and preserved evidence, so that a green contaminated worktree cannot claim completion.
26. As a human operator, I want hostile tests for stale identities, stale capabilities, forged evidence, deleted workspaces, interrupted processes, and controller termination, so that fail-closed behavior is demonstrated.
27. As a future agent, I want all decisions, specifications, tickets, evidence, failures, and recovery actions stored in the repository or project-local records, so that I can reconstruct the work without chat history.

## Implementation Decisions

- Extend the existing controller lifecycle rather than creating a parallel authority model.
- Use the existing event log and reducer as the durable lifecycle boundary. Recovery, abandonment, revocation, maintenance, and break-glass actions are append-only events.
- Keep immutable approved intent and historical graph versions separate from mutable execution state and derived projections.
- Add explicit human-only operations for abandon/recover, maintenance activation, break-glass activation, and fresh-cycle start.
- A disrupted worker is never resumed. Recovery marks the prior execution abandoned or preserves its terminal failure state, then creates a fresh execution identity.
- Recovery may dispose of only disposable worker workspaces and derived projections. It must preserve durable intent, event history, evidence, telemetry, execution records, failed outputs, and Git history.
- Recovery must verify event integrity and source authority before rebuilding state. It must fail closed if durable records are malformed, contradictory, or tampered with.
- Stale capabilities are rejected by execution identity, lifecycle generation, controller version, and/or explicit revocation records as appropriate to the existing authorization model.
- Recovery ends in `READY`; starting BUILD is a separate explicit human action.
- Maintenance freezes ordinary execution, snapshots state, preserves the known-good controller identity, creates a dedicated repair environment, and requires regression plus recovery proof before activation.
- Break-glass remains independent and human-only. It records controller SHA, unique nonce, reason, snapshot, repair environment, approval, proof, and append-only activation/exit records. Agents cannot invoke or approve it.
- Bounded BUILD, TEST, and VERIFY workers retain fresh isolated processes, exact context packets, scoped capabilities, and no ambient project skills or context.
- The project-aware controller may use project-local documentation, skills, durable state, and source material to reconstruct and coordinate work.
- Complete runtime registration and acceptance coverage for the project-local skill workflow. Resolve drift where generic current-branch implementation guidance conflicts with approved isolated execution.
- Do not rewrite accepted evidence or retroactively promote forensic I-1001 artifacts into acceptance proof.
- Implementation must follow the dependency-aware tickets produced by `/to-tickets`, blockers first, with each ticket implemented through fresh `/implement` executions using `/tdd` and ending in independent Standards and Spec review.

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior at the highest existing seams: controller lifecycle operations, durable event reconstruction, authorization decisions, worker adapters, CLI/skill entry points, and fresh-environment acceptance harnesses.
- Every behavior change begins with a failing regression or acceptance test, followed by the minimum implementation, then refactoring while green.
- Add positive and hostile tests for each lifecycle transition and authority boundary.
- Test interruption, failure, explicit abandonment, controller/process termination, repeated recovery, malformed/tampered durable state, stale capabilities, stale Prime/controller identities, workspace disposal, and new execution identity creation.
- Test maintenance freeze/repair/activation/exit and break-glass activation/rejection/exit with human-only enforcement.
- Test that immutable intent/history and all prior evidence remain reconstructable after recovery.
- Test that no worker can invoke or approve recovery, maintenance, or break-glass.
- Use clean disposable project directories and fresh processes for lifecycle acceptance. Do not treat ordinary in-place unit tests as complete proof.
- Preserve exact commands, outputs, runtime/model provenance, identities, changed-path manifests, evidence hashes, and failure artifacts in repository-local evidence.
- Reuse prior art in `control/events`, `control/authorization`, `control/operational.py`, existing restart/reconstruction tests, Stage B–E5 evidence, and the operational failure fixtures, while treating unaccepted or drifted artifacts as constraints rather than proof.
- Completion requires independent verification of the clean lifecycle, not only the repository test suite.

## Out of Scope

- Salvaging or productizing the disposable game workload.
- Deleting `.idd/` or rewriting historical evidence to make a run appear successful.
- Weakening worker isolation, granting workers ambient skills, or giving agents human-only authority.
- Replacing the existing architecture with a new control plane.
- Global Prime, Codex, or unrelated host configuration changes.
- Claiming parallelism, replanning, project-local knowledge, maintenance, or break-glass is complete without its own implementation and clean proof.

## Further Notes

The accepted audit establishes E5 as the last trusted frozen bounded milestone. E6/E7 and I-1001 remain useful evidence with documented drift and limitations, not an end-to-end completion claim. The route is: freeze the executable Skills Baseline, complete single-EU lifecycle and recovery, prove maintenance and break-glass, complete integration/promotion, then address later capabilities and final clean completion proof. All failed and superseded attempts remain part of the forensic record.
